description: AICPA Trust Services Criteria — contract requirements for vendors processing customer data systems.

snippets.text: Vendor must maintain a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Security Trust Services Criterion, with the report covering at least the most recent twelve (12) month period and made available to Customer upon request.

Vendor must implement role-based access controls, multi-factor authentication for privileged access, and quarterly access reviews. Any access to Customer data must be logged and retained for at least one (1) year.
Vendor must follow a documented change management process that includes peer review, testing in non-production environments, and rollback procedures for all changes to systems handling Customer data.
Vendor must maintain an incident response plan and notify Customer of any security incident affecting Customer data within seventy-two (72) hours of detection.
Customer data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256 or equivalent. Encryption keys must be managed in a dedicated key management system.
Vendor must perform annual risk assessments of its own subprocessors that handle Customer data, and disclose its subprocessor list to Customer.
Vendor must collect, monitor, and retain security-relevant logs for systems handling Customer data, with log retention of at least one (1) year and alerting on anomalous events.
Vendor must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan with documented Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO), tested at least annually.
